scope: Test stage (08-test.md), document stage (09-document.md) and 00-intro.md of the recorded Claude Sonnet 5.5 inline run of node-fix-bug (ShipLoop 1.3.0 / plugin 2.3.1): test = 3 tool calls, 18 s; document = 2 tool calls, 8 s, of 223 s and 70 turns. Code claims were checked at main da9e2e75 (1.5.0): rendered node-fix-bug offline packets (packets.py offline_packets), shiploop_test_loop, shiploop_mutation, shiploop_item_scope, shiploop_lint, shiploop_navigator, shiploop_loops, test/shiploop_e2e/run.py SEED_SCRIPT, and two read-only probes (a temp repo from the node-base fixture: base run and mutation check). The intro table puts test 3rd-4th by size (verify 23,663, step-plan 22,292, carry-forward 20,908, test 19,013), not the longest. Salesforce live2 events.jsonl read for the reporter question only.

findings.observation: Every `complete` the model ran from step-plan on was typed `... 2>&1 | head -N` (N 12 to 60; the test packet came out of the Improve step's `complete ... | head -30`). `shiploop_status_hook._verb` returns None for any piped command, so the status hook never sees them (owner rule: hooks see every command). The test packet reached the model as 4,863 of 24,571 chars (7 of 7 over-limit packets after step-plan reached it at 3,385 to 7,361 chars of 17,134 to 28,804). It opened no file, ran its own `git stash push -q src/paginate.js ... git stash pop -q` instead of the printed `red-check`, and the RULES bullet 'Run ShipLoop commands in the foreground, unpiped' (in the 28,966-char step-plan packet it received whole) did not stop the first piped call. On main's rendered test head (14,605 chars, about 132 lines) `head -30` shows 3,671 chars and drops Full packet, the Until Loop block, red-check, RULES and the Result template.
findings.proposal: Add one line directly under the callback in `_first_callback_lines` (at least three suites pin the callback's lead text, so add a line, do not reword): `Run it as printed, with no pipe, redirect or head: its output is the next stage's instructions and a cut hides them.` Same line under the Improve callback variants. Do not rely on another RULES bullet (plan 3.2(d)). Add `piped_shiploop_calls` (ShipLoop CLI calls whose command contains `|`) to metrics.py and arms.py; keep the line only if it falls below the A/A spread.
findings.risk: About +115 chars in the first 3 lines of every producer and Improve packet (offset: TD-2's deleted sentence). A model habit may not change: unproven until the metric shows it.
findings.plan_ref: 3.2(d) (a RULES bullet is the lever that already failed here); 1.0(b)/1.2 budget characters, not lines
findings.est_effect: Not estimated. Targets the cut that hid the loop start, red-check, pointer, RULES and template in every producer stage after step-plan; main's head hides more than the 1.3.0 head did.

findings.where: shiploop_navigator.packet_head (position of `_after_status_lines` and of `Full packet:`); shiploop_navigator.render (whole print)
findings.observation: `packet_head` appends `_after_status_lines` (Optional-fields note, Until Loop block, red-check line) last, although its docstring says 'directly after the status block'. Rendered test head: `Full packet:` at line 94, `INVOKE /until-loop` at 103, `red-check:` at 121 of about 132, behind 6,440 chars of duties. A packet at or under 16,000 chars prints whole through `render`, which puts duties at line 96 and RULES at 114 of 125 (document) and the Until Loop at 52. Under the observed 12 to 40 line cut neither layout shows what to run or how to write the result.
findings.proposal: In `packet_head` emit `*_after_status_lines(...)` right after `narrative_lines` and before 'Current stage guidance:'. Print the pointer as the 3rd line, keeping the literal prefix: `Full packet: <path> (the request, quoted knowledge and run rules; read it with a file-reading tool, not the shell)`. Delete the sentence 'The duties and rules above are this stage's; the full packet adds the original request, the knowledge files and hand-offs it builds on, and the run rules.' as the same-stage offset. Give `render` the same order for loop stages (loop block and duties before References and quotes). Test: for every stage x route the first 40 lines hold the callback, Goal, status block, the loop Start line and the Full packet path.
findings.risk: The status hook reads the first 16,000 bytes: the status block stays ahead of the loop block (it ends near char 2,500). Position pins in packet-recut and PrintedHeadTests change. A move, not an addition.
findings.est_effect: 0 net bytes; INVOKE from line 103 to about line 18, red-check from 121 to about line 38 of the test head.

findings.observation: All three test-stage gates were silent no-ops here: tests/...-base1.md and ...-mutation1.md say 'skipped: no item base was recorded' yet carry `disposition: passed`, and the floor lost its base term. `_test_loop_gate` discards the summary lines each gate returns ('base: skipped (...)', 'mutation: skipped (...)'), and `complete --check-only` prints a fixed sentence, so neither the model nor the owner can tell a proof from a skip. Checked-by claims tests that only load the code are refused, and its '`complete --check-only` prints every refusal first' is false (the check-only path raises at the first failing gate).
findings.proposal: Collect the lines `base_check`, `loop_run` and `mutation_check` return and print them under the accept, and after the check-only sentence: `Gates: base [focused] ... -> red (3 ran, 1 failed) | candidate ... | mutation: skipped (no mutants: no changed product line matched an operator)`. Write `disposition: "skipped"` (keep `passed: true`) in `_base_run` and `mutation._check` when `skipped` is set, and count skipped gate records in metrics.py and fidelity.py (they already read dispositions) so a green run cannot hide an unrun gate. Shorten the canned check-only sentence to pay for it.
findings.risk: Tests pin complete's stdout; the lines print first, so a head cut still shows them. Readers use `passed` and read `disposition` only for 'could-not-run' (test_loop.refused_runs, latest_attempt_could_not_run, metrics.py), so 'skipped' with passed true is read as before.
findings.est_effect: About +250 chars per test complete; ends the guess about which gates ran.

findings.observation: Even with an item base the mutation gate cannot judge this fix. Probe (temp repo from the node-base fixture, `lint.capture_base`, fix applied, TC-1 appended): `candidates()` returns 0 for the changed line `const pages = Math.ceil(items.length / size);` (record: 'no mutants: no changed product line matched an operator') and 8 for unchanged lines. The base run on the same repo read node's spec output and went red as required (focused ran 3, failed 1; regression ran 8, failed 1), equal to the model's own stash result (pass 2, fail 1).
findings.proposal: Add language-neutral operators to `OPERATORS`: ("arithmetic", r"(?<=[\w)\]]) / (?=[\w(\[])", " * ") with its "*" to "/" mirror, and ("logical", r"&&", "||") with ("logical", r"\|\|", "&&") (and word and/or). Measured with only the `/` rule added: 1 candidate on the changed line and TC-1 kills it (killed 1, survived 0). Keep 'refuse only when a mutant ran and none was killed'; add no threshold.
findings.risk: More mutants raise the chance of a survivors-only sample on a good test (equivalent mutants), which refuses; the 8-sample spread and the no-threshold rule bound it. Python `//` is masked as a comment by `_mask` (existing limit).
findings.est_effect: A skipped gate becomes a judged one for call-name and arithmetic fixes; about 0.1 s per mutant here.

findings.observation: `SEED_SCRIPT` advances the run with `nav.apply` and `nav.save`, bypassing `_transition`, so `lint.on_transition` never calls `capture_base` and lint/items/W1.md does not exist in any seeded slice. In this run that disabled the base run, the mutation gate, the floor's base term, the verify change inventory (packet: 'No change inventory recorded for W1 (no base snapshot was captured when W1 started)') and the document skip rule (`item_scope.changed_paths` returns None, so document is always issued). The case still reports PASS. The real Salesforce run did capture a base (red-check text: 'lint base a09119813ed5').
findings.proposal: In `SEED_SCRIPT`, once the `plan` step has set `work_items`, write the item base: `for rel, text in lint.capture_base(run_dir, Path(state['repo']), item['id']).items(): store.atomic_write_text(run_dir / rel, text)` (or run each step through `nav._transition` and `nav.save(run_dir, after, writes)`). Add to shiploop-e2e-slice.test.py: lint/items/<id>.md exists after seeding. Add a 'gates not exercised' line to packets.py or fidelity.py listing any tests/*-base*.md or *-mutation*.md with `skipped`.
findings.risk: Seeded cases then run the real gates: expect new refusals (floor, base) until their fixtures are right; re-take the A/A baseline after the change.
findings.est_effect: No minutes. Makes every step slice a test of the test stage, the inventory and the document rule.

findings.where: shiploop_loops.WORK['test'] and REPEAT['test']; the comment in shiploop_navigator._loop_lines
findings.observation: The step-plan and test-spec Work lines end 'then run the `complete --check-only` command printed there and fix each refusal'; the test Work line does not, and no exit condition names the base proof, mutation or check-only. `_loop_lines` says the list 'ends with the red-check command the test loop's work runs before done', which the Work text never says. Commands and order are spread over duty 4, Checked-by and the late `red-check:` line; the model reached the right order (loop start, tests, check-only, loop done, complete) from memory of earlier stages.
findings.proposal: WORK['test']: append `; then run the `complete --check-only` command printed there (it runs the base run, the candidate run and the mutation check without counting) and fix each refusal.` REPEAT['test']: change `or a lint finding,` to `a lint finding or a check-only refusal,`. Correct the `_loop_lines` comment.
findings.risk: Changes the test loop contract text for new runs only (none in flight); `shiploop-loops` pins WORK text.
findings.est_effect: About +150 chars in the Argument; no new command.

findings.observation: In the rendered test packet `red_na` appears 5 times and the `[{"id", "reason"}]` shape 4 times (the 'Optional at test:' line, duty 6, BASE_RULE, FLOOR_RULE); the Optional line and duty 6 are both in the printed head. Checked-by says 'Base run below' and 'reach its floor, below', but the printed head carries none of COUNT/FLOOR/BASE_RULE (1,699 chars, full packet only), so 'below' points at nothing there.
findings.proposal: Delete the 'Optional at test:' line from `_template_note_lines` (about 330 chars): duty 6 states both fields and their shapes in the same head. In BASE_RULE and FLOOR_RULE replace the repeated shapes with '(shape: duty 6)'. Either print the three rules in the head after the red-check line (plan 1.2 P1 'floors, Base-run') or change 'below' to 'in the full packet'.
findings.risk: About 230 literal pins; confirm each pin's obligation is still carried (G-LEDGER) before converting it.
findings.est_effect: About -330 chars of head and -250 chars of tail.

findings.where: shiploop_prompts duty 1 of the document stage; shiploop_lint.on_transition and shiploop_quality.STAGE (inventory at verify); shiploop_item_scope.changed_paths
findings.observation: Document duty 1 says 'List the changed public behaviours from the change inventory', but the inventory is first recorded when verify is entered, so it does not exist at document and the document packet prints none. The model grepped README instead and wrote its result in the same call, before it saw the grep (it then said 'I'll fix my result's wording and finish').
findings.proposal: Print one script-derived line in the document packet from `item_scope.changed_paths(root, item)`: `Changed since the item base (script-derived): src/paginate.js, test/paginate.test.js` (or `not computed: <reason>`), and reword duty 1 to '1. **List** the changed public behaviours from the changed paths above, the step plan, the implement results and the item's diff.'
findings.risk: About +120 chars and a pin on duty 1; the line is data and skips nothing.
findings.est_effect: Saves the model's own search; removes a pointer to a file that does not exist yet.

findings.observation: Document is decided by a script, not the model: `_document_entry` records it not applicable only when the item's real diff touches no code or test path (`behavioural` = any path outside the `non_behavioural` classes). A bug fix that touches src and test always issues it. Here it was ceremony: 8 s, 2 tool calls, a 17,439-char packet (5,647 printed), result 'No docs affected', loop exit 2 vacuous. With no item base `changed_paths` is None, so it would also have been issued for a docs-only diff. The intro's 'document only for a behavioural change' means this path-class test.
findings.proposal: No new skip. Keep the script proof (section 10 forbids a model-judged skip), take the cost out with W2's dedupe and TD-8's derived line, and reword the intro line to 'when the diff touches code or tests'.
findings.est_effect: None; document was 8 s of 223 s here.

findings.observation: The test packet prints 'Refused runs for this action so far: 0 of 11 (base and candidate runs together); after that the item goes back to its step plan (revise).' That is a model-facing cap, which owner rule 7 and plan principle 8 rule out, and it is inaccurate: mutation refusals count too (mutation_check's own message says 'base, candidate and mutation runs together').
findings.proposal: Print the count only when it is above 0 and without the cap: `Refused runs for this action so far: N (base, candidate and mutation runs together).` Keep the cap and `_cap_refusal` script-side, which names the route out when it fires. Owner to confirm whether the 2026-10-10 refusal cap was meant to be model-visible.
findings.risk: If the owner wants the cap visible this is a no-op; showing the limit may invite giving up early, which is the reason for the rule.

findings.where: shiploop_test_counts readers; shiploop_test_loop._explain_base; references/platforms/*.md; plan D-25
findings.observation: Node: the gates read this project's output (candidate record: focused counts ran 3, ids_missing []; regression ran 8; in the probe the base run read the spec reporter and went red), so no adapter is needed for it. Salesforce live2 shows the need: the first red-check said 'sf apex run test ... --result-format human -> unread' (the table prints `Pass`, which `_PASS_LINE` does not read), and Grok wrote tests/rules_gate.sh to rewrite `Pass` to `PASSED` and to run `sf project deploy start` first, because `sf apex run test` does not deploy the working tree, so a local change cannot fail on the base. Plan evidence 14 records the refusal of that deploy as the block.
findings.proposal: Keep D-25 separate but raise it; before an adapter: (a) `_explain_base`'s 'unread' text names 'the platform card under references/platforms/' instead of listing node, pytest, jest and unittest; (b) each platform card states its reporter flag and whether the base run can observe its tests (org-bound tests cannot unless the command deploys the tree); (c) the adapter declares reporter vocabulary and 'run against the base' in one platform row.
findings.generic_ok: yes; platform detail only in references/platforms/
findings.risk: (a) and (b) are text. The Salesforce reporter flag is unverified here (sf never run): check it against fake_sf.
findings.est_effect: Removes a model-written wrapper and the unrequested deploy that blocked live2.

findings.where: shiploop_prompts duty 2 of the test stage; the test `summary` placeholder in `_result_template`
findings.observation: Duty 2 asks the summary to state 'which decisions you retain, refine or supersede and why' and the step plan's locators in evidence_refs. The submitted summary restates counts ShipLoop records in tests/*.md ('8 pass, 0 fail', 'it fails (1 fail)') and states no decision; evidence_refs holds only the loop receipt. No gate reads either, and the next packets list the step-plan result by symbol anyway.
findings.proposal: Test `summary` placeholder: `<tests added by ID and what each asserts; test decisions retained, refined or superseded and why; any test changed to pass a run and its independent reason; ShipLoop's records hold the counts>`. Delete 'locators and the step plan's in evidence_refs' from duty 2 (the next packet prints those paths).
findings.risk: Low; confirm with G-LEDGER that the decision obligation stays.
findings.est_effect: About -70 chars of duty; fewer restated facts in the summary.

works_well: Goal, Done when and Checked by sit in the first 5 lines, so the model did the whole stage from 4.9k printed chars: 3 calls, 18 s, check-only accepted, real complete accepted first try ('ShipLoop check-only: every script gate for test accepts this result').
`complete --check-only` is a free dry run of the base, candidate and mutation gates; used once, accepted. Keep it.

The count readers handle this project's reporter: candidate record focused `counts: {ran: 3, runners: [node]}`, `ids_missing: []`, `npm test` ran 8; in the probe the base run read the same output and went red (3 ran, 1 failed), matching the model's own stash check.
The next packet lists the gate records as symbols ('W1 test base run: RUN/tests/...-base1.md', candidate, mutation, loop receipt): a script-derived evidence trail the model does not have to type.

Document's skip is a script proof over the real diff (`_document_entry`), not a model claim; its exit 'each changed document was reread after the last edit' is what made the model correct its own wrong statement in the same stage.
not_measured: Whether the status hook and keepalive fired on the piped completes (no hook log in the artifact); `_verb` says they do not bind.
A cleared model after a line-cut print (S-6 arm); this warm run finished from memory of earlier stages.
A real run's mutation outcome on a changed line that matches an operator (only the probe; the artifact's gate was skipped).
The Salesforce test stage end to end (live2 ended BLOCKED there) and the sf reporter flag candidates.

Time effect of any proposal: test 18 s and document 8 s of 223 s leave little to save on this case.
